issues.description: The template's Main.java shows instantiation of Seal, Pig, and Goat using two-argument constructors (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), implying animals require two constructor parameters. However, the problem statement/UML describes animals with only a name attribute (and instructs constructors to initialize class attributes), and the reference solution implements each animal with a single-argument constructor (String name). This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature for the animal classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template and problem statement with the intended single-parameter constructors: update the commented instantiations in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use one-argument constructors (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if a second attribute was intended, update the UML/problem statement to include that attribute and ensure all animal classes (and the solution) provide constructors accepting both parameters.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal subclasses: the template's Main.java invokes Seal, Pig, and Goat with two arguments (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem statement and solution implementation define/expect single-argument constructors that only initialize the name (e.g. Seal(String name)). This API/name mismatch between the starter template and the described/solution classes can confuse students about the required constructor signature and which attributes the classes should initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the starter template calls consistent with the problem statement and solution: update src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to instantiate animals with a single String name (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")), or alternatively adjust the class constructors in the solution and problem to accept and document the second parameter if that attribute is intended.
